security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, or DOT graph edges rather than executable behavior. The remaining risk is contextual: SDK templates encourage broad Write, Bash, npx, and permission-bypass patterns without enough safety guidance.

remediation.issue: SDK examples enable broad tool access.
remediation.suggestion: Show safer defaults with prompt-on-use permissions, minimal allowed tools, command allowlists, and workspace limits before including Bash or Write.

remediation.issue: MCP server launch command lacks validation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Document that package names, versions, environment values, and network access must be reviewed before running npx-based MCP servers.

remediation.issue: Permission bypass appears in the process diagram without a warning.
remediation.suggestion: Label bypassPermissions as unsafe for marketplace templates and advise against it outside controlled local testing.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent agents that encode domain rules and workflows. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through agent design, SDK setup, testing, and packaging.
actual_capabilities: Provides a four-phase SOP for agent research, specification, architecture, and technical enhancement.
Defines system prompt sections for identity, commands, tools, workflows, guardrails, and success criteria.
Includes TypeScript and Python Claude Agent SDK implementation examples.
Documents MCP integration, memory namespace patterns, and cross-agent coordination concepts.
Guides validation with typical cases, edge cases, error cases, integration cases, and performance checks.
limitations: Does not implement a complete runnable agent by itself.
Requires users to verify current SDK APIs, package versions, and local environment settings.
Needs security review before enabling Bash, Write, MCP servers, or broad permission modes.
Works best when domain research and example tasks are already available.

use_cases.title: Build a specialist coding agent
use_cases.description: Create an agent that understands a project stack, coding standards, workflows, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Standardize operational agents
use_cases.description: Turn repeated business workflows into consistent agents with documented inputs, outputs, and guardrails.

use_cases.title: Design coordinated agent systems
use_cases.description: Plan agents that share memory, coordinate tasks, and report progress through defined MCP patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single-role agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-creator to design a specialist agent for [role]. Include purpose, boundaries, core tasks, required knowledge, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an existing agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to refine an agent prompt.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent prompt with agent-creator. Strengthen its domain knowledge, failure modes, validation checks, and output format.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an SDK-ready agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-creator to convert this specification into an SDK-ready agent plan with tools, permissions, tests, and packaging notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-agent workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-creator to define a multi-agent workflow for [process]. Include agent roles, handoffs, memory keys, escalation rules, and validation gates.

output_examples.input: Create a customer support triage agent for a SaaS product.
output_examples.output: A structured agent plan with role definition, triage categories, escalation rules, response standards, validation checks, and packaging tasks.

output_examples.input: Improve a debugging agent that gives inconsistent recommendations.
output_examples.output: A revised prompt plan with clearer diagnostic steps, evidence requirements, failure modes, test cases, and success criteria.

output_examples.input: Plan a workflow with research, writing, and review agents.
output_examples.output: A coordination design with each agent role, handoff protocol, shared memory naming, progress reporting, and review gates.

best_practices: Start with domain research before writing the system prompt.
Define guardrails, failure modes, and validation checks before implementation.
Use minimal tool permissions and review any command-capable integration.
anti_patterns: Do not create generic agents without domain-specific examples and boundaries.
Do not enable broad Bash, Write, or bypass permissions without explicit review.
Do not skip testing for edge cases, error handling, and output consistency.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates structured plans, prompts, examples, and implementation guidance for specialized AI agents.

faq.question: Does it generate runnable agent code?
faq.answer: It includes SDK examples, but users must adapt and verify code for their current environment.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it suitable for multi-agent systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes coordination, MCP integration, memory naming, handoff, and validation guidance.

faq.question: What security review is needed?
faq.answer: Review tool permissions, Bash access, Write access, MCP server commands, and any permission bypass settings.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you need repeatable agent behavior for engineering, operations, research, or platform workflows.
